summary: Controlled 2026 evaluations show that agent-interface choices interact with model capability and task type; a model name or global score alone is an incomplete unit of advice.

points.text: In Fan et al.’s matched 128k-context harness, Nemotron-3 30B resolved 25.2% of SWE-bench Verified tasks with predefined tools versus 10.2% with bash-only. Nemotron-3 550B reversed the ordering: 65.8% with predefined tools versus 69.4% with bash-only, at lower cost. Both SWE-bench tool comparisons were significant under the authors’ paired test.

The same study found planning raised the 30B model’s SWE-bench success by 11.6 percentage points while increasing cost; for the 550B and Mistral 128B models it mainly cut cost with small decreases in success. Advice must name the optimization target.

CoreCodeBench, an ACL 2026 paper, tested 1,524 tasks from 12 Python repositories and found model ranking shifts between development, bug fixing and test-driven implementation. A single coding index misses these differences.
ContextBench evaluated four frontier models and five coding agents on gold-context issue tasks; agent setup and context selection matter alongside the base model.
